### 🟢 Approval recommended It is a self-contained, test-only change whose assertions I verified against the doctor Port-check logic, and it follows the established loopback free-port test convention with proper fixture cleanup. **No open issues** 🎉
What changed in this PR This PR makes two doctor custom-port tests deterministic. Previously `accepts custom port` and `passed is true when no failures` hardcoded ports 59123/59124 and assumed nothing on the host held them, so an unrelated listener could redden an otherwise-green PR. The tests now take ownership of the port state by binding an OS-assigned port on `127.0.0.1` (the same address `doctor.js` probes), and add companion tests covering the `warn` branch deterministically. **Changes:** - Add small `holdPort`/`closeServer`/`freePort` helpers that reserve or hold an OS-assigned loopback port instead of using fixed literals. - Rewrite `accepts custom port` and `passed is true when no failures` to use a freshly freed port, and add two new tests asserting a bound port reports `warn` and does not by itself fail the run. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | packages/​server/​tests/​doctor.test.js | Replaces hardcoded ports with OS-assigned loopback ports via new helpers and adds deterministic `warn`-branch coverage for the doctor Port check. |
Review effort: Balanced
